precepts.text: Israel is a holy people whom the Most High chose to be a special people above all people on the face of the earth.
precepts.point: She blessed the Most High who delighted in Solomon to set him on the throne of Israel, because the Most High loved Israel forever; even the nations understood that the Most High chose Israel above all people.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

Even the nations understood that the Most High chose Israel above all people. The queen of Sheba said it herself: “Blessed be the Lord thy God, which delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king, to do judgment and justice.”

She saw it in Solomon's servants too: “Happy are thy men, happy are these thy servants, which stand continually before thee, and that hear thy wisdom.” They were happy to be in order, serving with joyfulness and not complaining, because Solomon ruled wisely and took care of his people.

precepts.text: He set his love on Israel not because they were many but because he loved them and kept the oath to their fathers.
precepts.point: She blessed the Most High who delighted in Solomon to set him on the throne of Israel, because the Most High loved Israel forever; even the nations understood that the Most High chose Israel above all people.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

precepts.why:
“The Lord did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people: But because the Lord loved you, and because he would keep the oath which he had sworn unto your fathers, hath the Lord brought you out with a mighty hand”.

He set his love on Israel not because they were many, but because he loved them and kept the oath to their fathers. That is the love the queen of Sheba spoke of: “because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king”.

precepts.text: The tithe turned to money could be bestowed for whatsoever the soul lusteth after, meaning oxen, sheep, wine, and food, not sex.
precepts.point: Nothing is said of her being pregnant. The Ethiopian tradition claims Solomon fathered a son with her and founded a dynasty, but the scripture gives no such thing; she turned and went to her own country with her servants.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

precepts.why:
When the way was too long to carry the tithe, Israel could turn it into money, “And thou shalt bestow that money for whatsoever thy soul lusteth after, for oxen, or for sheep, or for wine, or for strong drink, or for whatsoever thy soul desireth: and thou shalt eat there before the Lord thy God, and thou shalt rejoice”. Whatsoever the soul lusteth after means oxen, sheep, wine and food, not sex. The word desire in scripture does not always mean what people think.

So when “king Solomon gave unto the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked”, people assume it was sexual. But her desire was to know his wisdom and see his order.

Nothing is said of her being pregnant. The Ethiopian tradition claims Solomon fathered a son with her and founded a dynasty, but the scripture gives no such thing: “So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.”

precepts.text: Make no idols nor graven image to bow down to, so the lions in Solomon's house were not for worship.
precepts.point: All Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were pure gold; silver was nothing accounted of in his days. Once in three years the navy of Tarshish brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

precepts.why:
“Ye shall make you no idols nor graven image, neither rear you up a standing image, neither shall ye set up any image of stone in your land, to bow down unto it: for I am the Lord your God.” The law forbids images set up to worship.

Solomon's throne had six steps, “and two lions stood beside the stays.” “And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps: there was not the like made in any kingdom.” These standing lions were not graven images to bow down to. They were not worshipped, so the lions in Solomon's house were not for worship.

precepts.text: The same yearly weight of gold coming to Solomon is recorded, showing this is the compressed retelling of the fuller history.
precepts.point: Solomon makes two hundred targets and three hundred shields of beaten gold and puts them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

precepts.why:
“Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred threescore and six talents of gold.” Kings records the same yearly weight of gold that Chronicles gives: six hundred sixty and six talents.

Chronicles is the compressed retelling of the fuller history in Kings. The same gold, beside what the merchants and the kings of Arabia and the governors brought, went into the two hundred targets and three hundred shields of beaten gold that Solomon put in the house of the forest of Lebanon.

points: When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Most High, she came to prove him with hard questions, and came to Jerusalem with a great train, camels bearing spices, much gold, and precious stones.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: She communed with him of all that was in her heart, and Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hid from the king that he told her not.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: When the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon's wisdom, the house he built, the meat of his table, the sitting of his servants, their apparel, his cupbearers, and his ascent to the house of the Most High, there was no more spirit in her.

Everything in the kingdom was in order, the servants in uniform, the cupbearers in place; this is why order matters in the body today, so that those who come in are astonished and the worldly spirit of disorder leaves them, seeing the discipline and love for the people.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: She told the king the report she heard in her own land was true, that she had not believed it until her eyes had seen it, and behold the half was not told her; his wisdom and prosperity exceeded the fame she heard.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: She said happy are his men and servants that stand continually before him and hear his wisdom; they were happy to be in order, serving with joyfulness and not complaining, because Solomon ruled wisely and took care of his people.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: She blessed the Most High who delighted in Solomon to set him on the throne of Israel, because the Most High loved Israel forever; even the nations understood that the Most High chose Israel above all people.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: She gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and spices in great store, and precious stones; and the navy of Hiram brought from Ophir great plenty of almug trees and precious stones, of which Solomon made pillars for the house of the Most High and harps and psalteries for singers.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked. People assume this was sexual, but her desire was to know his wisdom and see his order; the word desire in scripture does not always mean what people think, as the law shows the tithe money could be spent on whatever the soul lusted after, meaning oxen, sheep, wine, and food.

Nothing is said of her being pregnant. The Ethiopian tradition claims Solomon fathered a son with her and founded a dynasty, but the scripture gives no such thing; she turned and went to her own country with her servants.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: The weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents, besides that of the merchants and the kings of Arabia and the governors. He made two hundred targets and three hundred shields of beaten gold, and a great throne of ivory overlaid with the best gold.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: The throne had six steps, a round top, stays on either side, and two lions by the stays with twelve lions on the six steps, such as was not made in any kingdom. These standing lions were not graven images to bow down to; the law forbids images set up to worship, but these were not worshipped.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: All Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were pure gold; silver was nothing accounted of in his days. Once in three years the navy of Tarshish brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and wisdom, and all the earth sought him to hear the wisdom the Most High put in his heart, bringing presents year by year. No king reigned like Solomon or was richer than him.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: He gathered a thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, placed in the cities and at Jerusalem; these were of his own people, so he provided jobs for them rather than making them slaves.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

points: He made silver in Jerusalem as stones, and had horses and linen yarn brought out of Egypt; a chariot came up for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Solomon bought the best of everything, but there comes a point where riches and power can pervert the mind if a man is not grounded, and that is what begins to happen.
